questions.question: In an undirected triangle graph, what is the degree of each node?
questions.explanation: Each of the three nodes connects to the other two, so every row of the adjacency matrix has two ones.

questions.question: Which data structure does breadth-first search use to visit neighbors layer by layer?
options: A LIFO stack only
A sorted list of edge weights
The graph Laplacian
A FIFO queue
questions.explanation: BFS enqueues newly discovered nodes and removes the oldest first. That ordering completes one distance layer before the next.

questions.question: What does the graph Laplacian L=D-A reveal through its zero eigenvalues?
options: The number of connected components
The number of directed edges only
The largest node feature value
The graph's average path length exactly
questions.explanation: The multiplicity of eigenvalue zero equals the number of connected components for an undirected graph.

questions.question: What is the purpose of multiplying node features by normalized adjacency in one GNN message-passing round?
options: To remove every edge from the graph
To aggregate information from neighboring nodes with controlled scale
To sort nodes by their labels
To compute a Fourier transform of each feature
questions.explanation: A normalized adjacency mixes neighboring feature vectors while limiting degree-dependent magnitude growth. A learned linear map or nonlinearity can follow the aggregation.

questions.question: How does spectral clustering use the Fiedler vector?
options: It assigns every node to the component with the largest degree
It uses the largest adjacency eigenvalue as a node label
It splits nodes by the signs or thresholded values of the Laplacian's second-smallest eigenvector
It removes the second row of the adjacency matrix
questions.explanation: The Fiedler vector captures the smoothest nonconstant partition direction. Thresholding it often separates weakly connected groups.

questions.question: What changes when an edge (u,v) in a directed graph is reversed to (v,u)?
options: Nothing; directed edges are always symmetric
Every node degree doubles
The graph becomes a complete graph
Reachability and adjacency entries can change because the reverse edge is not implied
questions.explanation: Directed adjacency need not be symmetric. Reversing one edge changes which node receives an outgoing connection and can alter traversal results.
